title: Sounds of Onam: Keeping the Chenda beat alive in Chennai
content:
As Onam approaches, the thunderous rhythms of Chenda Melam evoke the sounds of Kerala’s temple festivals. In Chennai’s Villivakkam, Sri Sastha Kshetra Vadya Sangam at Ayyappan Kovil, has been keeping the tradition alive and accessible through free Chenda classes that attract learners across generations.
The institution was founded by Rajeev Kumar, whose association with the temple began in his childhood. His father, C.N. Sukumaran Guruswamy, founded the Villivakkam Ayyappan Temple. The idea for the institution emerged during preparations for the temple’s second Kumbhabhishekam in 2013, when Rajeev’s father expressed a desire to have an in-house Chenda troupe, as bringing teams from Kerala was expensive. Inspired by the idea, Rajeev decided to learn the Chenda. He trained under guru Devaraj Marar for two years.
Though Rajeev was fortunate to have found a guru in the city, the experience made him realise how difficult it was for aspiring Chenda players in Chennai to receive a formal training. “Not everyone can afford to travel to Kerala and stay there to . “That bothered me, and I decided to start an institution,” says Rajeev.
Rajeev, under the guidance of his father, established Sri Sastha Kshetra Vadya Sangam as a charitable trust with a simple objective: make Chenda Melam accessible to anyone interested in learning it, regardless of gender or language. Rajeev teaches in Tamil, English and Malayalam, and says offering free classes remains integral to the institution’s purpose. “We don’t run this organisation for money. We run it as a service,” he says.
New students begin with Chembada Thalam, which Rajeev describes as a basic form. Then, they progress to Panchaari Melam and Adantha Melam. Rajeev says learning the basics takes around four to five months. An arangetram is held for the students every December. The institution is preparing for its 10th batch in 2026 and has so far had nearly 150 students.
The learners include young boys and girls, and even middle-aged men and women. Shankar A. and R. Karthick conduct the Chenda classes, while S. Surendar organises events, teams and manages various activities.
For Shankar, teaching involves breaking the course into smaller sections so students can understand and practise each part before putting them together. Regular practice, he adds, helps improve concentration and makes lessons easier to learn.
Rhythm is central to Chenda Melam. Rajeev explains that the tala used is similar to what is used in Carnatic percussion. Rhythm lies at the heart of Chenda Melam. Rajeev explains that its rhythmic structure is similar to that of Carnatic percussion, though the presentation differs. The performance incorporates a range of talas, including Chembada, Adantha and Panchaari, each contributing to its distinctive sound
Chenda Melam brings together a range of instruments, including the chenda, ezhathalam, kombu, idakka and kuzhal, with diverse talas and rhythmic patterns forming its musical framework. The institution’s efforts, says Rajeev, have been sustained by the positive response from both students and parents. “Once the training is completed, we take our students to perform at festivals and events across Chennai,” he adds.
Younger learners say they were first drawn to the instrument’s powerful sound. Ten-year-old T. Nikhil, who has already completed his arangetram, recalls being fascinated with the chenda when he saw it being played at the temple. “I now enjoy playing it,” he says. Eight-year-old Jeevitesh shares a similar story.
The institution has also given women an opportunity to learn an art form that was not always accessible to them. Says 49-year-old Sini Sreekrishnan, “I wanted to learn it since childhood. Whenever I pick up the instrument and play, I am transported to Kerala.” She also appreciates the inclusive environment at the Sangam. “There is no discrimination on the basis of gender or age here.”
As Onam approaches, the work at Sri Sastha Kshetra Vadya Sangam in Villivakkam offers a reminder that Kerala’s musical traditions can thrive well beyond the State’s borders. By creating opportunities for people of all ages and backgrounds to learn and perform, it is ensuring that the resonant rhythms of Chenda Melam continue to find new audiences and practitioners.

title: From Mexico City to Santiago to Beijing, Years of Culture initiative outlines summer programme
content:
Qatar's Years of Culture (YoC) initiative, the country's long-term cultural exchange programme, is marking a vibrant summer of international programming, with major exhibitions in Mexico, Chile and China bringing Qatar's creative partnerships to audiences across the world.
Spanning multiple continents, the programme reflects the growing international reach of the Years of Culture initiative and its commitment to building lasting relationships.
From football and the shared memories of the FIFA World Cup in Mexico City, to contemporary cinema and video art in Santiago, and Qatar's Bedouin heritage in Beijing, each project offers a distinct perspective on the country while creating new opportunities for intercultural dialogue.
Adviser to the Years of Culture initiative for Latin America, Mohammed Jassim al-Kuwari, said the programme was founded on a simple principle: enduring relationships are built over time through mutual understanding.
"This summer brings that idea to life," he said. "In Mexico, we are building new connections through this year's cultural partnership; in Chile, we are continuing to nurture relationships established last year; and in China, a project first launched as part of a previous Year of Culture is reaching a new audience.”
“These programmes create opportunities for people to come closer together and gain a deeper understanding of one another through culture,” he said.
Four years after Qatar hosted the FIFA World Cup Qatar 2022 – becoming the first Arab country to stage the tournament – Mexico hosted the World Cup as one of the tournament's host nations.
Against this backdrop, two exhibitions in Mexico City used football to explore how sporting moments can tell deeper stories about culture, identity and the connections between people.
Organised by the 3-2-1 Qatar Olympic and Sports Museum and Museo Jumex, “Pieces of Glory: Iconic Moments in Football History” traced more than a century of the sport through objects associated with some of its most memorable moments, including items linked to legendary players such as Pele and Diego Maradona.
Elsewhere in the city, at the Centre for Digital Culture, “Towards Glory: The Legacy of Qatar 2022” turned its focus to the FIFA World Cup Qatar 2022.
Through archival material, photographs, multimedia installations, personal testimonies and tournament memorabilia, the exhibition revisited the 2022 World Cup as a defining moment when millions of people encountered Qatar and the wider Arab world.
In Chile, meanwhile, the summer programme poses a different question: what remains after an official year of partnership comes to an end.
The cultural relationships established during the Qatar-Argentina-Chile 2025 Year of Culture have continued to develop, building on connections forged through shared experiences of migration, storytelling and cinema.
At Santiago's Centro Cultural La Moneda, the exhibition “Our Ghosts, Your Ghosts: Promising Visions for a Radical Cinema” opened this month in its Latin American debut.
The exhibition brings together films and video works by artists and filmmakers from the Arab world, Africa and Southeast Asia, exploring themes of memory, displacement, identity and belonging across cultures and geographies.
The exhibition features works from the collections of Mathaf: Arab Museum of Modern Art and the future Art Mill Museum, alongside contributions from the Doha Film Institute.
It also advances a broader proposition: that cinema and video are integral to the history of contemporary art, and that this history becomes richer when it incorporates voices and perspectives that have often been marginalised by dominant narratives.
For the Years of Culture initiative, however, Santiago represents more than an exhibition venue.
"The arrival of the exhibition in Santiago embodies an important principle at the heart of the Years of Culture initiative: the end of a partnership year does not mean the end of the relationships," al-Kuwari said.
That principle has become increasingly central to the initiative.
Cultural exchange is measured not only by what takes place during a designated year, but also by the opportunities and possibilities that emerge after it ends.
In China, at the National Museum of China in Beijing, “Nomadic Life Reimagined”, organised by the National Museum of Qatar (NMoQ), introduces visitors to the knowledge, traditions and ways of life that shaped Qatar's Bedouin and semi-nomadic past.
The exhibition explores life in Qatar from the 18th century until the discovery of oil, a period when mobility and nomadism were essential to understanding the landscape and the means of survival within it.
Objects, photographs, films and oral histories highlight the skills and traditions that developed in response to this environment, including tentmaking, Al Sadu weaving, relationships with animals, and the knowledge required to navigate and survive in the desert.
The exhibition itself has become rooted in the concept of movement and mobility.
It was first developed as part of the Qatar-Middle East, North Africa and South Asia 2022 Year of Culture and presented at the NMoQ alongside the FIFA World Cup Qatar 2022.
Two years later, it travelled to the National Museum of Mongolia.
This summer, it has arrived in Beijing through a collaboration between the NMoQ and the National Museum of China.
Since its launch in 2012, the Years of Culture initiative has expanded across a broad range of fields, including exhibitions, heritage, design, photography, cinema, sport, education and community programmes.
Its annual partnerships provide a starting point for cultural exchange, while the initiative's impact extends beyond the end of each designated year through the relationships, projects and new opportunities that emerge from them.
From football in Mexico City to cinema in Santiago and Qatar's nomadic heritage in Beijing, this summer's programme demonstrates the initiative's evolving approach to cultural diplomacy – one in which a single exhibition can become the beginning, rather than the conclusion, of a lasting international relationship. – QNA

title: Comunidade se une e paga salários de funcionários de pizzaria tradicional destruída por incêndio
content:
Comunidade se une e paga salários de funcionários de pizzaria tradicional destruída por incêndio
Moradores e clientes se uniram para ajudar a pagar os salários dos funcionários de uma pizzaria que funciona há mais de 50 anos, foi atingida por um incêndio e teve que fechar as portas. A comunidade de Minneapolis, nos Estados Unidos, arrecadou milhares de dólares para garantir que a casa volte a funcionar e os funcionários possam se manter até lá.
A mobilização começou depois que a Jakeeno’s Pizza & Pasta, que passou de pai para filhas – e é administrada pelas irmãs Patty e Amy Keegan – foi atingida por um incêndio em 11 de julho, no sul de Minneapolis, no estado de Minnesota. “Queremos eles de volta. Nós os valorizamos. É terrível que tenham perdido o trabalho por causa disso, então estamos tentando manter todo mundo amparado”, disse ela à CBS Minnesota.
A pizzaria é tão querida na região que o empresário Bob Tinsley criou uma campanha de arrecadação no GoFundMe e já conseguiu arrecadar US$ 22,6 mil (mais de R$ 116 mil) para ajudar cozinheiros, garçons, bartenders e outros trabalhadores a atravessar o período sem renda.
Tradição de mais de 50 anos
A Jakeeno’s Pizza & Pasta funciona há mais de cinco décadas em Minneapolis. É um restaurante familiar.
A pizzaria foi fundada em 1975 por Jack e Carol Keegan e, anos depois, passou a ser administrada pelas filhas Patty e Amy.
Ao longo da história, o restaurante enfrentou momentos difíceis, como a crise financeira, a pandemia de Covid-19 e os impactos dos protestos que aconteceram na região após a morte de George Floyd, por policiais.

- Menina de 9 anos pede para doar mochila a colega que usava uma rasgada, em Salvador; vídeo
O incêndio
O fogo atingiu o telhado da pizzaria na manhã de 11 de julho. Os bombeiros precisaram abrir diferentes pontos da cobertura para controlar as chamas.
O restaurante estava vazio naquele momento e ninguém ficou ferido. Mesmo assim, fumaça e destroços atingiram áreas internas e obrigaram o estabelecimento a suspender as atividades enquanto passa por reparos.
Agora, quem ajuda a pizzaria a atravessar mais um momento complicado são justamente os clientes e vizinhos que frequentam o local há anos.
Manter a equipe unida
A notícia boa é que as obras da reforma estão em andamento.
Patty Keegan contou que a principal preocupação hoje é conseguir manter a equipe unida para quando o restaurante reabrir.
Além das doações, moradores também podem apoiar o negócio comprando molhos e pizzas congeladas da marca, vendidos em mercados e cooperativas locais.

title: 2 Planes With The Same Flight Number Avoid Possible Disaster Thanks To Quick-Thinking Controller
content:
A potential disaster was averted Friday when a Phoenix air traffic controller recognized two American Airlines jets mistakenly were flying the same flight number and acted quickly to avoid confusion and keep them a safe distance apart.
Audio of the incident shortly after midnight Friday shows how he found a solution to ensure the planes that were both called American 2482 maintained proper separation as one plane arrived from Chicago shortly after the other had taken off in Phoenix.
“I’ve been working air traffic for 25 years. I’ve never seen two aircraft pretty much merge with the same call sign. That’s pretty incredible,” the controller said after the departing plane had safely cleared the area.
If both pilots thought the controller was telling them to fly at the same altitude as they headed toward each other, they might have collided, so it was crucial they knew which plane he was directing.
Quick Thinking Ensured The Controller’s Instructions Were Clear
The audio posted by ATC.com shows how the controller quickly started referring to “American 2482 on the arrival” and “American 2482 on the departure” to keep the two planes straight.
The controller kept the arriving plane safely above the departing plane even as their flight paths converged and made sure that the pilots of both airlines saw each other when they were still miles apart. He also directed the departing plane not to climb too high, so a gap would remain between the planes.
The arriving pilot complimented the controller for his “nice work” once the two planes had passed each other safely.
“It could have been disastrous, but I’m glad it worked out,” the controller replied.
Expert Says Airline Must Have Missed That The Flights Would Overlap
Aviation safety expert Steve Arroyo said it’s likely that someone inside the airline’s dispatch center failed to catch that both planes would be in the air at the same time with identical flight numbers when both the dispatcher and the pilots signed off on the flight plan.
“You can drop the ball and that shouldn’t happen, but it’s nice to see that the system is resilient and we have all the safeguards,” said Arroyo, who has only seen this type of issue a couple times in his four decades with United Airlines. Arroyo started his career as a dispatcher before becoming a pilot.
Flight 2482 is a round-trip route that often flies back and forth between Chicago and Phoenix. Typically the same plane goes back and forth, but the flight out of Chicago was delayed by weather, so American found a second plane in Phoenix and that flight left on time. The result was that both planes briefly shared the same airspace before the arriving flight landed.
The Government And Airline Will Determine How This Occurred
The Federal Aviation Administration and American Airlines will investigate how this happened, and they both emphasized how glad they were that everyone remained safe.
“The diligence and professionalism of air traffic controllers and our pilots ensured required separation was always maintained and the issue was identified and addressed. Both flights continued safely and without incident,” American Airlines said in a statement.

title: Generative Artificial Intelligence (AI)-Assisted Self-Diagnosis and the Patient-Physician Relationship: Mixed Methods Study of Calibration, Participation, and Trust.
content: Patients increasingly use generative AI to interpret symptoms and seek health information, yet limited evidence shows how AI-assisted self-diagnosis is integrated into care-seeking and related to clinical interactions and patient-physician relationships. This study examined how AI-assisted self-diagnosis is incorporated into care-seeking processes and how it relates to patient participation in clinical encounters and trust in physicians. An exploratory sequential mixed methods design was used. In the qualitative phase, Chinese adults who had used generative AI to interpret symptoms, appraise possible conditions, or seek health advice within the previous year were purposively recruited through Xiaohongshu, WeChat Moments, and WeChat groups. Semistructured interviews were conducted from August 20, 2025, to January 10, 2026, and analyzed using reflexive thematic analysis. In the quantitative phase, an anonymous web-based survey was conducted in China through Huixiang Data from January 25, 2026, through January 28, 2026. Adults who had used generative AI for health consultation involving symptom interpretation or preliminary self-diagnosis within the previous 6 months were recruited through convenience sampling. Measures included perceived AI-assisted self-diagnosis quality, calibrated illness appraisal, patient participation, diagnosis validation, diagnosis comprehension, trust in physicians, AI use frequency, trust in health information sources, and demographic characteristics. Trust in physicians was assessed using 5 adapted items covering competence, integrity, and benevolence. Descriptive statistics, Pearson correlations, and PROCESS mediation analyses were performed. Qualitative findings (n=48) indicated that AI-assisted self-diagnosis was commonly used in a prediagnostic gray zone for preliminary orientation, informal triage, and interim self-management. Participants described AI as helping them appraise illness severity, prepare for consultations, ask questions, and understand physicians' diagnoses and reasoning. Quantitative findings (n=546) were consistent with these patterns. Perceived AI quality was positively associated with calibrated illness appraisal (b=0.57, 95% CI 0.49-0.64), which was positively associated with patient participation (b=0.35, 95% CI 0.28-0.43). The indirect association was significant (estimate=0.20, 95% bootstrap CI 0.14-0.26). Perceived AI quality was also associated with diagnosis validation (b=0.69, 95% CI 0.61-0.76) and diagnosis comprehension (b=0.65, 95% CI 0.58-0.73), which were associated with trust in physicians (b=0.15, 95% CI 0.07-0.23 and b=0.20, 95% CI 0.12-0.28, respectively). The corresponding indirect associations were 0.10 (95% bootstrap CI 0.04-0.17) through diagnosis validation and 0.13 (95% bootstrap CI 0.07-0.19) through diagnosis comprehension. Generative AI may function as an informational intermediary across the care-seeking process rather than undermine medical authority. By supporting illness appraisal, consultation preparation, and postconsultation understanding, AI-assisted self-diagnosis may be associated with greater patient participation and trust in physicians.

title: Effects of the Empowering Coaching™ training program on the coach created motivational climate, psychological need satisfaction and team cohesion
content: IntroductionThis study examined the longitudinal effects of a coach education program (based on Empowering Coaching™), implemented in a school-based setting across the sport season, on young athletes’ perceptions of the motivational climate, satisfaction of basic psychological needs, and team cohesion across a sport season.MethodsParticipants were 314 athletes from Mexico (12–16 years, M = 15.11, SD = 1.30) at baseline, of whom 143 completed post-intervention assessments (45.5% retention). Twenty-five coaches engaged in workshops and guided reflections over a 7-month period. Athletes completed questionnaires assessing the prevailing motivational climate, need satisfaction, and cohesion at the beginning and end of the season.ResultsPaired-sample analyses revealed significant small-to-moderate improvements in athletes’ perceptions of an empowering climate, autonomy and relatedness satisfaction, and social cohesion, whereas competence satisfaction and task cohesion showed no significant change. To further examine hypothesized mechanisms, structural equation modeling indicated that perceptions of an empowering climate directly predicted changes in task cohesion and indirectly predicted social cohesion through changes in autonomy satisfaction.DiscussionThe findings highlight the potential of an extended, collaborative and multi-activity delivery of Empowering Coaching™ training to promote young athletes’ feelings of autonomy and belonging as well as group functioning within competitive school sport.

title: NT passes voluntary assisted dying laws
content:
NT passes voluntary assisted dying laws
The Northern Territory Parliament passed on Thursday a bill legalising voluntary assisted dying (VAD) in a conscience vote, completing the set for legality throughout Australia.
Several Country Liberal Party backbenchers crossed the floor to vote for changes to their party’s own Rights of the Terminally Ill Bill but ultimately failed to get the numbers, with Cabinet ministers voting as a block despite it being notionally a conscience vote (NTN).
An amendment was tabled to remove the 12-month prognosis time frame for VAD eligibility, but it was ultimately unsuccessful (ABC).
Other unsuccessful amendments included a push to bring the laws in line with expert advice, to remove the doctor gag clause, and to ensure minimum requirements for conscientious objectors (NTN).
The NT is now both the first and last Australian jurisdiction to legislate for VAD after a 1995 law was overturned by the Commonwealth two years later (ABC).

title: Machine Learning-Guided Personalized Immunochemotherapy Strategies in Intrahepatic Cholangiocarcinoma.
content: Immunochemotherapy (IO-chemo) has become standard care for patients with unresectable intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma (iCCA), but benefit of adding IO varies greatly among individuals. We sought to develop a system to identify patients most likely to benefit from this treatment based on individualized treatment effect (ITE) estimation. This study included patients with unresectable iCCA who underwent either IO-chemo or chemotherapy alone (chemo). Patients were enrolled from three discovery and seven external validation centers. Target trial emulation was employed to obtain unbiased average treatment effect estimation, and a causal machine-learning model was used to estimate heterogeneous treatment effects for IO-chemo. Based on predicted ITE, patients were stratified into high-benefit, no- to moderate-benefit, and negative-benefit groups, with overall survival used as the primary end point. The discovery cohort included 1485 patients; the external validation cohort included 562 patients. In the high-benefit group, compared with chemo, the hazard ratio (HR) for IO-chemo was 0.39 (95% CI, 0.30-0.52; p < 0.001), with mortality reduced by 24.1%, 31.2%, and 28.5% at 12, 24, and 36 months, respectively. In the no- to moderate-benefit group, IO-chemo did not differ from chemo (HR, 0.91; 95% CI, 0.70-1.18; p = 0.488). In the group with negative predicted ITEs, IO-chemo was associated with shorter OS than chemo (HR, 1.91; 95% CI, 1.47-2.48; p < 0.001). In the external validation cohort, the corresponding HRs were 0.45 (95% CI, 0.30-0.68; p < 0.001), 0.62 (95% CI, 0.42-0.93; p = 0.018), and 1.93 (95% CI, 1.28-2.91; p = 0.002), respectively. A causal machine learning-based model can estimate individualized treatment effects of immunochemotherapy in patients with unresectable intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma, enabling clinically meaningful benefit stratification. The overarching goal of intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma (iCCA) management is to deploy biomarkers that identify patients most likely to benefit from immunochemotherapy and thus enable personalized therapy, but little research has examined how clinicians choose between chemotherapy and immunochemotherapy beyond head-to-head efficacy comparisons or efforts to define subgroups suited to a single regimen. Built on a causal machine-learning (ML) framework, the Causal ML-Guided Personalized Immunochemotherapy Strategies in Intrahepatic Cholangiocarcinoma model described here offers a validated, clinically practical tool to quantify the benefit of immunochemotherapy in iCCA. In this study, 17 clinical variables were used to reliably identify patients most likely to benefit from immunochemotherapy and to predict long-term survival. By focusing on individualized treatment effects rather than average treatment effects, the model provides a strong foundation for future trials that seek to operationalize intelligent treatment selection and pushes precision immunochemotherapy for iCCA closer to routine practice. title: Freno al ICE en California: la prohibición judicial de operativos protege a solo algunos templos
content:
Freno al ICE en California: la prohibición judicial de operativos protege a solo algunos templos
El Cuarto Circuito mantuvo una orden preliminar limitada a entidades demandantes, con excepciones para arrestos con orden y situaciones de emergencia
- 4 minutos de lectura'
Una corte federal de apelaciones ratificó una prohibición que impide a los agentes del Servicio de Inmigración y Control de Aduanas (ICE, por sus siglas en inglés) realizar operativos de inmigración dentro de ciertas iglesias. La protección no ampara a todos los edificios, sino exclusivamente a los templos que forman parte de la demanda judicial en Sacramento, en California.
Qué establece el fallo del Cuarto Circuito sobre operativos del ICE en lugares de culto
En enero de 2025, el gobierno eliminó las restricciones de operaciones del ICE en lugares sensibles, que incluían iglesias, escuelas y hospitales. La decisión repercutió en una disminución de casi el 40% de la asistencia en ciertos templos debido al temor de la comunidad migrante. Por este motivo, una coalición de grupos religiosos inició un litigio judicial que la semana pasada tuvo una nueva determinación.
El 18 de agosto, el Tribunal de Apelaciones del Cuarto Circuito de Estados Unidos decidió mantener vigente la orden judicial preliminar de un tribunal de distrito mientras el caso continúa.
En la opinión del tribunal de apelaciones, redactada por la jueza Barbara Milano Keenan, los lugares de culto demostraron que la política del Departamento de Seguridad Nacional (DHS, por sus siglas en inglés) supone una carga sustancial para el libre ejercicio de su religión.
En concreto, la jueza escribió que “la nueva política está teniendo un efecto disuasorio en sus congregaciones y ya ha provocado una disminución en la asistencia”.
La demanda fue presentada por la Cooperative Baptist Fellowship —presta servicios a aproximadamente 750.000 bautistas—; el Gurdwara Sahib West Sacramento —atiende a 30.000 personas-; y las siguientes seis congregaciones cuáqueras:
- New York Yearly Meeting of the Religious Society of Friends.
- Philadelphia Yearly Meeting of the Religious Society of Friends.
- New England Yearly Meeting of the Religious Society of Friends.
- Baltimore Yearly Meeting of the Religious Society of Friends.
- Adelphi Friends Meeting of the Religious Society of Friends.
- Richmond Friends Meeting of the Religious Society of Friends.
De esta manera, el ICE no podrá realizar operativos por el momento en las instalaciones de las organizaciones mencionadas.
Por qué otras iglesias deberán iniciar sus propios litigios para limitar operativos migratorios
De acuerdo con la política implementada por la administración del presidente Donald Trump el año pasado, los agentes del ICE deberían usar su criterio y una “buena dosis de sentido común” al decidir si llevar a cabo acciones de control migratorio en esos lugares sensibles.
El cambio eliminó las directrices que aplicaba la administración de Joe Biden que prohibían las acciones de control migratorio en o cerca de áreas protegidas como lugares de culto, escuelas u hospitales.
Aunque la resolución del tribunal de apelaciones emitida el 18 de agosto solo protege actualmente a los templos demandantes directos —como el Sikh Temple Sacramento—, expertos y abogados aseguran que este fallo establece un precedente.
En un comunicado citado por CBS News, los demandantes adelantaron que continuarán con los procesos legales para mitigar el alcance de la política y proteger a los feligreses.
“Esta decisión reafirma una promesa fundamental de la libertad religiosa: toda persona debería poder reunirse, practicar su culto, rezar y servir a su comunidad sin temor a que las autoridades de inmigración perturben ilegalmente los espacios sagrados”, escribieron.
Detenciones del ICE en California: el 74% de los inmigrantes bajo custodia no tiene antecedentes penales
El 2025 estuvo marcado por redadas del ICE en diferentes partes del país norteamericano, con grandes operativos en Los Ángeles desde el pasado junio. Pese a que durante los siguientes meses la acción de control migratorio pasó más desapercibida, las cifras de arrestos y deportaciones en el estado aumentaron este año.
En el Estado Dorado, de acuerdo con un informe compartido por Los Angeles Times, tres de cada cuatro personas bajo custodia no tienen antecedentes penales. En concreto, los inmigrantes sin antecedentes penales representan el 74% de la población diaria promedio en los centros de detención de California y el 79% a nivel nacional.
En centros específicos como el de Adelanto, solo el 38% tiene antecedentes, y en California City esta cifra cae al 25%.

title: Mobile queen conch hatcheries strive to help the species, engage Caribbean communities
content:
- International demand for queen conch meat and shells has led to severe overharvesting, while habitat degradation, pollution and warming waters add further threats.
- In a bid to slow the decline of the queen conch, researchers are partnering with local conservation organizations across the Caribbean to establish a network of mobile hatcheries aimed at protecting the giant marine snail through its vulnerable early life stages.
- The goal is not only to nurture developing conch, but to create community spaces where local people can learn about the queen conch life cycle and participate in restoration efforts.
- However, some researchers have doubts about whether aquaculture alone can restore wild conch fisheries.
Queen conch were once so abundant that fishers in many parts of the Caribbean could wade into knee-deep waters and gather armfuls of the pink, whorled shells. Today, however, the giant marine snails are in decline across the Gulf of Mexico and the Caribbean Sea, while some populations have already collapsed.
Growing demand for queen conch (Aliger gigas) meat and shells has led to overharvesting; habitat degradation, pollution and warming waters add further threats. Despite a 1992 CITES Appendix II listing to regulate their international trade, seasonal restrictions and bans by several Caribbean countries to address overfishing and juvenile harvesting, and a 2024 designation as a threatened species under the U.S. Endangered Species Act, few queen conch survive to adulthood compared to historical baselines.
In a bid to slow the species’ decline by helping more conch reach reproductive age, scientists are deploying an innovative set of solar-powered mobile hatcheries to shelter them through their vulnerable early life stages. The Queen Conch Lab (QCL), affiliated with Florida Atlantic University (FAU) in the U.S., partners with local conservation organizations to deploy the hatcheries. The aim is not just to build nurseries that will nurture and protect developing conch, but to create community learning spaces where students and other visitors can gain knowledge about the species’ life cycle and participate in restoration efforts, according to Megan Davis, director of the QCL and a research professor at FAU’s Harbor Branch Oceanographic Institute.
“By bridging aquaculture, fishery, conservation and restoration all in one place [at the mobile hatchery], the local community gains an understanding of all the aspects needed for good management of the conch species,” Davis told Mongabay by email.
In June, QCL’s eighth mobile lab, on the island of Eleuthera, Bahamas, celebrated its first hatch and plans to release up to 2,000 juvenile conch per year. That number is large, but a 2022 study published in Fisheries Science & Aquaculture found that only one in 4,000 to 10,000 juveniles typically survives to adulthood, hindering the species’ ability to replenish its numbers. According to the study, predation by other marine animals drives much of the high mortality of juvenile conch, followed by fishing of underage conch and the disturbance of their shallow-water nurseries by environmental and climate-related stressors.
Hatcheries inspiring hope
During spawning season, an adult female queen conch produces an egg mass containing hundreds of thousands of eggs. After fertilization, the larvae undergo a 21-day development cycle, floating in the ocean before metamorphosing into juvenile conch and settling on the sea floor. But surviving through these early life stages is challenging — and that’s where the QLC mobile hatcheries come in.
First, fishers find a female queen conch and collect about a quarter of its total egg mass. Back at the lab, the harvested eggs incubate for four to five days. After hatching, thousands of small veligers — plankton-sized larvae — feed on phytoplankton also grown in the hatchery.
Once ready for metamorphosis, staff place them on trays submerged in seawater with seagrass blades containing diatoms — their favorite food while living on the seafloor — cuing them for transformation from free-swimming larvae to their more recognizable crawling snail form. Two months later, the staff will transfer them to sand-bottom trays to grow another 8-9 centimeters (3-3.5 inches).
At a year old, the juvenile conch are moved out of the lab to protective acclimation pens for one to two months, where they grow accustomed to life back at sea before transferring to a wild conch nursery. It will be another two to three years before they reach adulthood.
Community connections
The mobile nature of the labs, which are about 8 feet wide and 20 feet long (2.4 meters by 6 meters), allows them to be easily shipped from Florida to Caribbean islands or towed to a more secure site in the event of a hurricane or other extreme weather. While the hatcheries utilize solar power, rising sea and air temperatures necessitate connecting to the local power grid during the hottest periods of the year, Davis said. This additional power source enables use of air-conditioning units, along with water chillers that cool the warmer seawater entering the hatchery’s larval tanks.
Since the first mobile lab launched in 2022, communities in Jamaica, Puerto Rico and the Bahamas have worked with the QCL to establish additional hatcheries, with more planned for Cataño, Puerto Rico; Fort Pierce, Florida; and Providenciales, Turks and Caicos Islands. Davis said interest has grown as she and her team showcase the hatcheries on social media and promote their vision for a regional network across the Caribbean.
Each hatchery employs two to three people. Local staff, some trained from scratch with no prior marine biology experience, maintain the labs and grow food for the conch, and manage visiting groups primarily from local schools.
The hatcheries, in Davis’ vision, function as educational resources for communities familiar with conch as a seafood product, but have not had opportunities to learn about the species’ life cycle or threats. “Sharing about the life cycle helps the community members know that a conch takes a long time to grow before it is (should be) fished,” she said.
Education, but not yet restoration
Andrew Kough, a research biologist at the Shedd Aquarium in Chicago, Illinois, in the U.S., and lead author of a 2025 review paper on conch aquaculture’s potential for wild population restoration, agrees that conch aquaculture, including the mobile hatcheries, provides a great opportunity for education and community engagement.
Up to now, though, no peer-reviewed research has supported the idea that aquaculture can substantively repopulate wild conch fisheries, Kough told Mongabay in a Zoom interview.
Kough views conch aquaculture as providing a useful symbol to help people connect with ocean conservation. “However, where that barrier seems to fall off is in the translation from taking that symbol and turning it into repopulation in the wild,” Kough said, adding that more research is needed to determine the impact of conch aquaculture on fisheries replenishment.
Davis, who co-authored a 2023 study with Kough on conch development, agrees on the need for further research. She said she’s hopeful the release of several thousand conch from a stationary hatchery in Curaçao in 2025 — along with a Jamaica mobile hatchery’s planned release of juveniles into protective enclosures later this year — will result in more conch reaching maturity and reproducing in the wild.
But ultimately, Davis contends the success of the mobile hatcheries is best measured by their ability to support community-driven conservation efforts. While the impact of restorative aquaculture efforts remains inconclusive, she said the hatcheries are important in showing that “there will always be a way to grow conch.”

title: Renewable Energy Is Winning, Trump Is Losing (Shocker!)
content:
Renewable Energy Is Winning, Trump Is Losing (Shocker!)
In a temporary blip of insanity, the US electorate failed to learn from its first mistake, and sailed President Donald J. Trump into office for the second time on Election Day 2024. Many are now shedding the bitter tears of buyers remorse. Too bad for them. Meanwhile, the all-important business of climate action continues apace despite Trump’s death cult focus on fossil fuels, with renewable energy resources now claiming 30% of power generating capacity in the US.
Renewable Energy Now At 30%…
The 30% figure comes from EIA, the US Energy Information Administration, an independent agency affiliated with the Department of Energy.
You can follow EIA here, but for those of us in a hurry an essential resource is Ken Bossong, whose Sun Day Campaign organization diligently summarizes EIA’s main renewable energy findings and emails to a list, upon which is CleanTechnica.
Typically I’ll share a nugget or two from one of those emails, but this one is so encouraging that it’s impossible to pick out a few highlights. The headline says it all:
“Over the Last Five Years, Solar Capacity Tripled, Batteries Grew 20-Fold & Wind Expanded 33%; Renewables Now Generate >30% of U.S. Electricity.”
“New data just released by the U.S. Energy Information Administration (EIA), and reviewed by the SUN DAY Campaign, reveal growth of almost 11% in electrical generation by renewable energy sources in the first half of 2026,” the Sun Day Campaign elaborates.
“Moreover, renewables and battery storage are projected to add about 82.9 gigawatts (GW) of new generating capacity in the U.S. by June 30, 2027 while total fossil fuel and nuclear power capacity will fall by almost 3.1-GW,” they add.
…And Trump Failed To Stop It.
If you caught that thing about fossil fuels and nuclear energy, yes that is a thing that is happening, or not, as the case may be. Despite Energy Secretary Wright’s heroic posturing, coal power plants are still on the downward slide (here’s a recent example), and killing off the coal mining workforce is not helping much in terms of a future revival.
Meanwhile, my inbox is flooded with news of this or that nuclear energy venture, which is all well and good except that nothing of much consequence will materialize in the near future, and by the time the farther future arrives it will be too late. Renewable energy, particularly in the form of solar plus storage, has a speed-to-power advantage that nuclear just can’t beat. Here’s the Sun Day Campaign on that topic:
“Over the last five years, installed utility-scale (i.e., >1 megawatt (MW)) solar capacity has tripled while small-scale solar (i.e., <1-MW) has more than doubled. Wind capacity has increased by nearly a third and utility-scale battery storage capacity has ballooned by almost 20-fold.”
And, here’s the kicker, which bears repeating:
“Electrical generation by renewables sources grew almost 11% and was more than 30% of the U.S. total in the first half of 2026.”
Digging further into the EIA details, the Sun Day Campaign notes that electricity from renewable energy during the first half of 2026 was 10.9% greater than in the first half of 2025.
“The growth was led by utility-scale solar (up 21.6%), small-scale solar (up 13.0%), hydropower (up 10.1%), and wind (up 6.5%),” the Sun Day Campaign elaborates. “The combination of just wind and solar, including small-scale solar, provided 22.3% of domestic electrical production.”
Meanwhile, output from nuclear power plants grew just 1.7% and natural gas grew only 1.8%, reflecting longer construction timelines and, in the case of gas power plants, a years-long backlog of turbine orders.
“Electricity produced by U.S. coal facilities fell by 11.3%,” the Sun Day Campaign emphasizes.
Twisting the knife a bit more, the Sun Day Campaign notes that the combination of wind and solar produced 58% more electricity coal power plants and 28% more than nuclear during the first half of this year.
Renewable Energy And Energy Storage Are Coming For Your Fossil Fuels
Trump’s war on wind power has produced some results that should warm the cockles of a fossil fuel stakeholder’s heart, but a fresh burst of activity in the solar field has made up the difference. “In June alone, solar-generated electricity was greater than that of either wind or hydropower, making it the leading renewable energy source for the month,” the Sun Day Campaign notes.
And, there’s plenty more where that came from, considering the fresh burst of activity on the domestic solar manufacturing side, which Trump himself recently stimulated with new limitations on imported polysilicon.
Here are some more news bites from the Sun Day Campaign (breaks added for readability):
Over the past year, renewable energy capacity increased by almost 45,000-MW.
Between July 1, 2025 and June 30, 2026, the installed capacity of utility-scale solar increased by 28,076.7-MW while that of small-scale solar and wind grew by 6,492.0-MW and 10,552.9-MW (including 800-MW of offshore wind) respectively.
The combined capacity of all renewable energy sources – including hydropower, biomass, and geothermal – expanded by 44,889.3-MW.
In addition, utility-scale battery energy storage capacity increased by 17,858.8-MW. [3]
Over the past decade, renewably-generated electricity has grown rapidly as solar capacity increased nine-fold and wind capacity more than doubled.
Underscoring the significant role of energy storage, the Sun Day Campaign draws attention to 2016, when storage capacity was so minuscule that EIA didn’t even bother to report it. Storage capacity grew to more than 2.6 gigawatts in 2021 before leaping to almost 51.7 gigawatts by June 30 of this year, an increase of almost 20-fold in the past five years.
Don’t Let The Door Hit You On Your Way Out
The Sun Day Campaign has lots more on the latest EIA report (follow them on bluesky here). As for what that means in action, take a look over at Texas. Despite its red state political profile, Texas emerged as a wind energy leader in the early 2000’s and went on to compete head-to-head with California and Florida for solar leadership, too.
The state’s energy storage industry has been no slouch, either. The Texas power grid was struggling to keep up with demand and weather-related incidents not too long ago, but the speed-to-power factor kicked in more recently, enabling the grid manager, ERCOT, to deploy more renewable energy and storage to fill the gap.
“The fuel mix in ERCOT from July 21-22 demonstrates how ERCOT utilized solar during daylight hours and shaved peak demand with discharge from battery energy storage systems,” Renewable Energy World reported on July 23 under the headline, “As Texas temperatures soar, ERCOT crushes demand and generation records without incident.”
Turning now to the state of federal energy policy under President Trump — oh, never mind. As the saying goes, you can’t make a silk purse out of a sow’s ear. They also say there’s a sucker born every minute, and they say you can fool some of the people some of the time — twice! — but you can’t full all of the people all the time…

title: Hong Kong unveils its first dedicated psychiatric facility for under-18s
content:
Hong Kong unveils its first dedicated psychiatric facility for under-18s
New site is part of wider redevelopment of city’s main psychiatric hospital to enhance service quality and foster recovery
Hong Kong’s main psychiatric hospital has unveiled the city’s first facility exclusively dedicated to child and adolescent patients, as part of a wider redevelopment that offers upgraded wards designed to enhance service quality and foster recovery.
The redevelopment of Kwai Chung Hospital has increased the total construction floor area from 80,000 to 134,000 square metres, ensuring it can provide 1,000 beds for psychiatric patients.
It also involved the reallocation of specialist outpatient clinics, day hospital facilities and inpatient services to new blocks.
“In psychiatry, the environment itself serves as a form of therapy,” Dr Cheng Koi-man, the hospital’s chief executive, said on Wednesday.
“Compared with the old hospital, this space creates an open, safe and community-like therapeutic environment while offering more indoor and outdoor spaces for inpatients, breaking the public’s stereotype of traditional and enclosed psychiatric management.”
The redeveloped campus includes a new main facility and a child and adolescent block, which is also Hong Kong’s only site dedicated to psychiatric care for patients under 18.

content:
Ethiopia Records Major Gains in Health Coverage, Local Production and Emergency Preparedness: Health Minister
Addis Ababa, August 25, 2026 (FMC) — Ethiopia has recorded major gains in health coverage, local production of health products and emergency preparedness, Health Minister Dr. Mekdes Daba said.
Addressing the 76th Session of the World Health Organization (WHO) Regional Committee for Africa in Addis Ababa, Dr. Mekdes said Ethiopia’s health-sector progress over the past decade has increasingly translated into measurable improvements in the lives of its people.
She said maternal mortality declined from 871 to 141 deaths per 100,000 live births, according to Ethiopia’s 2024–2025 Demographic and Health Survey, while under-five mortality fell from 67 to 51 deaths per 1,000 live births since 2016.
Child wasting also declined from 10% to 5% over the same period, while primary healthcare coverage increased from 64% to 86.3%, the minister said.
The scale of demand for healthcare has also expanded significantly, with more than 233 million outpatient visits recorded over a one-year period, she said.
Ethiopia’s health workforce has grown from 212,185 health professionals to about 325,000, while the total number of health-sector personnel, including support staff, has approached half a million, according to Dr. Mekdes.
She said the country has simultaneously expanded financial protection through community-based health insurance, which now covers more than 69 million people and has reached 91% of its targeted coverage.
“Health cannot be sustainable without financing it,” Dr. Mekdes said, calling for greater domestic resource mobilization, improved efficiency and stronger financial protection.
She said international partnerships remain important, but external support should help countries build lasting domestic capacity rather than create permanent dependency.
Ethiopia has also made significant progress in local production of medicines and other health products, with the domestic market share supplied by local manufacturers increasing from 8% to 44%, the minister said.
She added that the Ethiopian Food and Drug Authority (EFDA) has reached WHO Maturity Level 3, marking progress in strengthening the country’s regulatory capacity.
Dr. Mekdes described localization as more than an industrial policy, saying it has become an integral part of Ethiopia’s health-security strategy, particularly following the vulnerabilities exposed by the COVID-19 pandemic.
She also highlighted Ethiopia’s expansion of digital health systems, saying community health records under the Ethiopian Community Health Information System have grown from about 112,000 records seven years ago to coverage of around 7 million households, representing data on more than 33 million people.
The minister stressed that digital transformation must be guided by equity, ensuring that people in rural and remote communities benefit from technological advances as much as those in urban areas.
Ethiopia has further strengthened its capacity to detect and respond to public health emergencies, with outbreak detection capacity increasing from 65% to 95%, while rapid-response team coverage has risen from 75% to 93%, she said.
Dr. Mekdes said the experience of COVID-19 and other emergencies demonstrated that preparedness cannot be postponed until a crisis occurs.
She said preparedness must therefore become an integral part of the country’s health-system architecture, urging continued investment in emergency readiness.
Looking ahead, the minister said Ethiopia’s next phase of health-system transformation must place greater emphasis on quality alongside scale, with primary healthcare, communities and health workers remaining at the center of the effort.
She stressed that technology, financing, workforce development and local manufacturing should ultimately serve one objective: ensuring that every person can access the healthcare they need as close to home as possible.
Dr. Mekdes urged African countries to use the Regional Committee session not merely to adopt strategies, but to translate them into implementation, calling for greater investment in people, stronger primary healthcare systems, sustainable health financing, expanded local production, digital transformation and equitable access.
She said the success of Africa’s health systems should ultimately be measured not by the number of strategies adopted or technologies introduced, but by whether mothers receive care when needed, children are protected from preventable diseases and health workers have the tools required to serve their communities.
Dr. Mekdes called for greater African solidarity in building stronger and more resilient health systems, saying the continent’s health future would depend on collective action by its countries and institutions.

title: Energia | Helen avasi Eiranrantaan uuden lämpölaitoksen, mutta nyt katse on jo ydinvoimassa
content:
Älkää huoliko, kahvia ei ole keitetty jätevedestä, vitsailee termospullon äärellä Helenin toimitusjohtaja Olli Sirkka.
Hetkeä aiemmin tila-auto on kaahannut syvälle maan uumeniin Helsingin Eiranrannassa. Tänne, noin 45 metrin syvyyteen, on juuri avattu Helenin uusi lämpöpumppulaitos.
Munkkisaaressa sijaitseva laitos tuottaa jatkossa kaupunkilaisten tarpeisiin kaukolämpöä ja kaukojäähdytystä puhdistetun jäteveden hukkaenergiasta.
Vuosittain syntyy noin 300 gigawattituntia kaukolämpöä, mikä vastaa noin Rauman kokoisen kaupungin vuotuista lämmönkulutusta.
Helen luopui kivihiilen käytöstä energiantuotannossaan viime vuonna. Yhtiön tavoitteena on saavuttaa nettonollapäästöt ja irtautua polttoon perustuvasta energiantuotannosta vuoteen 2040 mennessä.
Uuden laitoksen avaaminen vie Helenin vähän lähemmäs tuota tavoitetta, Sirkka sanoo. Hänen mukaansa konkreettinen ja nopeasti näkyvä hyöty on, että tulevana talvena Salmisaaren voimalaitokselle tarvitsee tuoda lähes tuhat rekka-autollista vähemmän pellettejä poltettavaksi kuin aiemmin.
Investoinnin kokonaishintalappu oli 100 miljoonaa euroa, johon sisältyi työ - ja elinkeinoministeriön myöntämää EU-rahoitusta noin 14,5 miljoonaa euroa.
Valtion edustajana paikalla laitoksen avajaisissa on ympäristö- ja ilmastoministeri Sari Multala (kok). Suojakypärään ja huomioliiveihin pukeutunut ministeri hehkuttaa juhlapuheessaan, miten nyt ”eletään todeksi visiota hiilineutraalista Suomesta” ja kuinka uusi laitos on myös keskeinen osa huoltovarmuutta ja omavaraisuutta.
Laitoksessa energiaa voidaan ottaa talteen hyvin matalalämpöisestä, jopa viisiasteisesta vedestä. Samalla vähennetään Itämereen kohdistuvaa lämpökuormaa.
Jos vesi on lämpöpumpuille liian kylmää, sähkökattila voi lämmittää sen sopivaksi. Näin tuotanto toimii myös kaikkein kylmimpinä aikoina.
Niin, se sähkö.
Helen ilmoitti hiljattain nostavansa siirtohintaa noin seitsemän prosenttia lokakuun alusta alkaen, mikä näkyy suoraan helsinkiläisten sähkölaskuissa. Samalla sähkön määräaikaisten sopimusten hinnat ovat nousseet huomattavasti keväästä.
Miksi siirtohintaa nostettiin tilanteessa, jossa sähkön hinta on muutenkin korkealla?
Sirkan mukaan kyse oli käytännössä inflaatiokorotuksesta. Lisäksi Helsingin väkiluvun kasvaessa Helenin on jatkuvasti rakennettava lisää sähköverkkoa, mikä ei ole tiuhaan rakennetussa kaupungissa halpaa.
Koska investointitarve jatkuu, ei Sirkka pysty lupaamaan, ettei siirtomaksu nousisi entisestään lähivuosina. Ja koska sähkön markkinahintaa on mahdoton ennustaa, hän suosittelee etenkin sähkölämmittäjille kiinteää sähkösopimusta.
Eiranrannan uusi laitos voi kuitenkin osaltaan auttaa hintapiikkien tasaamisessa: sähkön ollessa kallista laitos voidaan ajaa vaikka kokonaan alas ja vapauttaa sähkö muuhun käyttöön, Sirkka kertoo.
Sirkan mukaan Helen pyrkii jatkuvasti tuottamaan lisää sähköä ja odottaa ”kieli pitkällä” uusia investointeja. Seuraavaksi kiikarit on suunnattu kohti ydinvoimaa.
Pienydinvoimalan rakentaminen on edellytys sille, että Helenin tavoite nettonollapäästöistä toteutuu, Sirkka sanoo. Ensimmäinen voimala voisi tulla Salmisaareen, Vuosaareen tai Östersundomiin, ja tavoitteena on, että se aloittaisi toimintansa 2030-luvun aikana.
Hankkeelle löytyy Sirkan mukaan poliittista tukea niin kaupungin kuin valtionkin suunnalta. Suurin haaste liittyy pitkään ja hitaaseen lupapolkuun.
”Pelkästään luvitukseen menee 7–8 vuotta, ja siinä voi olla vaikka minkälaisia vaiheita”, hän sanoo.
Keväällä hyväksytty uusi ydinvoimalaki pyrkii osittain helpottamaan tilannetta, sanoo ministeri Multala. Myös muuta byrokratiaa pyritään hänen mukaansa karsimaan turvallisuudesta tinkimättä.
Jos Helen haluaisi esimerkiksi rakentaa useamman ydinvoimalan, kaikille voitaisiin tehdä periaatepäätös samaan aikaan, vaikka rakentaminen tapahtuisi eri vaiheissa.
”Kaiken ei tarvitsisi olla vielä periaatepäätöksen kohdalla teknisesti lukkoon lyötyä”, Multala sanoo.

title: Kansai hosts final of Vietnamese language contest for younger generations
content:
HÀ NỘI – On the occasion of the 81st anniversary of the August Revolution (August 19, 1945-2026) and the National Day (September 2) of the Socialist Republic of Việt Nam, the “I Love My Mother Tongue” (Tôi yêu Tiếng nước tôi) contest’s final took place on August 23 in Higashi Osaka, Japan.
The event saw the participation of representatives from Vietnamese diplomatic missions, various associations, artists, parents, and the Vietnamese community living in the Kansai region.
The contest aims to preserve, practise, and promote the Vietnamese language within the Vietnamese community in Japan, with a particular focus on the younger generation born or raised in the host country. Furthermore, it serves to implement the Politburo’s Resolution No 23-NQ/TW, dated August 2, 2026 on the affairs related to overseas Vietnamese in the new era.
Aiming to create a platform for the community to use Vietnamese and to encourage families to maintain their native language, it also provides an opportunity for the younger generation to learn more about Vietnamese history, culture, and traditions, according to organisers.
A key highlight of the contest is the integration of language with expressive arts, rather than a simple test of linguistic knowledge. This allows participants to showcase their Vietnamese proficiency, individual talents, and personal feelings regarding their family, homeland, culture, and the Vietnamese people.
Twelve finalists were selected from the qualifying rounds to compete in the final stage, during which each contestant was given a maximum of four minutes to complete two performance categories. These performances were presented in Vietnamese through various creative formats, through which the judges evaluated the contestants' language proficiency, presentation skills, content, and emotional resonance.
Speaking at the event, the Vietnamese Consul General in Osaka, Nguyễn Trường Sơn, spoke highly of the contest's significance in fostering a Vietnamese-speaking environment in Japan, especially for children and youth who are born and educated in a Japanese-language environment.
“The Vietnamese language is more than just a tool for communication, it embodies historical values, culture, and national identity, serving as a vital bridge connecting overseas Vietnamese generations with their families and their homeland,” said Sơn.
The Consul General noted that preserving the mother tongue requires collective efforts from various stakeholders, including diplomatic missions, community associations, schools, and most importantly, individual families.
“Encouraging children to use Vietnamese in daily life and engaging them in language classes, cultural activities, and community platforms will ensure the language is maintained in a natural and sustainable way,” said Sơn.
Commending these efforts, he expressed his hope for more practical initiatives as such models would allow the younger generation to integrate successfully into Japanese society while remaining deeply rooted in their Vietnamese heritage.
According to Head of the Organising Committee, Lê Thương, a growing challenge for the Vietnamese community in Japan is the increasing number of children being born and raised entirely within the Japanese educational system. Without an environment for regular practice, their Vietnamese language proficiency risks declining across successive generations.
Consequently, language preservation efforts must be diversified and engaging, moving beyond the traditional classroom setting to spark genuine interest among learners.
"To translate policy into reality, we must start with concrete actions tailored to the community's needs. Whether it is a language class, a contest, an art performance, or a historical exploration activity, each serves to encourage children to use Vietnamese more frequently,” said Thương.
“The key is to create an environment where the language remains a constant presence in the lives of the younger generation."
She added that "I Love My Mother Tongue" also seeks to intertwine language with culture and history, ensuring that young people do more than just speak the language as they understand the profound values it conveys.
This approach also demonstrates how community organisations can implement the spirit of Resolution 23-NQ/TW at the grassroots level: by identifying practical issues facing the diaspora and developing sustainable, targeted programmes.
The event atmosphere was rich in Vietnamese identity, featuring a solemn flag-raising ceremony, vibrant Vietnamese-language performances, and moving stories of family and heritage shared across multiple generations.
For the overseas Vietnamese community, major national holidays serve as vital opportunities for the younger generation to explore their history and strengthen their bond with their homeland through activities adapted to their life in the host country. VNS

title: Gwangju Biennale restores ‘Taiwan’ name: report
content:
The Gwangju Biennale Foundation has agreed to allow Taiwan’s exhibitors to use the name “Taiwan” in the exhibition venue and in official documents and promotional materials, South Korea’s Munhwa Broadcasting Corp reported yesterday.
The foundation made the decision after considering Taiwan’s stance that it would withdraw from the exhibition, opening on Sept. 5th, if the name could not be used, the broadcaster said.
Earlier yesterday, the Ministry of Culture urged the foundation to respond by today to its request to restore the name of Taiwan’s participating exhibition from “NTMoFA,” the acronym for the National Taiwan Museum of Fine Arts, to “Taiwan Pavilion.”
Photo: CNA
In a statement, the ministry “sternly protested” the foundation’s and the Asia Culture Center’s (ACC) refusal to restore the name and what it described as efforts to prevent Taiwan Pavilion personnel from entering the venue to set up the exhibition, originally scheduled to begin on Tuesday last week.
The statement did not specify what action would be taken if the organizers failed to respond.
The ministry said it issued statements on Monday and Wednesday last week explaining that the name “Taiwan Pavilion” was changed to “NTMoFA” without discussion or prior notice.
It also pointed to a statement issued yesterday by the Taiwan Pavilion’s curator and artists, titled “You Must Change Your Name,” which accused the foundation of repeatedly ignoring the museum’s objections to the name change and said an artistic institution should not become a tool for suppressing self-identification.
Over the past week, the ACC has refused to allow Taiwanese exhibitors to enter the venue to set up the exhibition, citing the lack of an official document from the foundation, the ministry said.
Although the museum received a copy of a foundation letter permitting them to enter the venue on Wednesday, the ACC continued to say it had not received the document and refused to allow NTMoFA representatives to enter, the ministry said.
After a museum representative took photographs to document the incident, ACC venue staff demanded to inspect the person’s phone and asked them to delete the photographs, it said.
Furthermore, the foundation proposed relocating Taiwan’s exhibition to an alternative storage space that was much smaller than the original site, the ministry said.
Members of the international artist community and art workers have also spoken out, urging the foundation not to use its authority to determine the name under which participants are identified and to restore the name “Taiwan Pavilion” as soon as possible, it said.
Earlier, the foundation said it would neither intervene in nor censor the content or expression of exhibitions, and would continue negotiations to ensure that the NTMoFA’s exhibition proceeds as planned.
The foundation said the exhibition is purely an artistic partnership and that it has never intervened, nor would intervene, in the NTMoFA pavilion’s curation, selection of works, installation methods or the expressions of its curator and artists.
It said it was concerned that the controversy had developed into a political and diplomatic issue, adding that the dispute stemmed from differing interpretations of administrative procedures and the agreement concerning the pavilion’s participating institution and how it should be labeled in official materials.
The foundation said that the agreement signed on Jan. 12 clearly identified the Gwangju Biennale Foundation and the National Taiwan Museum of Fine Arts as the parties involved and that its implementation was based on that agreement.
In contrast, the ministry has insisted that the original agreement was that the name “Taiwan Pavilion” would be used and was only changed by the foundation in June.
The foundation argued that the labeling used in official documents and promotional materials should be distinguished from the exhibitor’s own self-identification.
Regarding the difficulties encountered by Taiwan’s exhibitors, the foundation said it had signed a contract with the venue for use of the exhibition space, but the contract did not specify the countries or institutions that would hold exhibitions there.
It said it would ask the ACC to open the space and cooperate with the installation and exhibition operations so that the NTMoFA’s exhibition can proceed as planned.
If further delays or difficulties arise, the NTMoFA could consider using an alternative space inside the biennale venue, it added.
The foundation concluded that both the autonomy of exhibitors and the official operations stipulated in the agreement should be respected, saying the priority was not for the two sides to “more loudly propagate their own stance,” but to quickly find a workable solution that would allow the exhibition to be held as scheduled.
Founded in 1995, the Gwangju Biennale in South Korea is Asia’s oldest and most prestigious biennial of contemporary art.
In an August titled “Who is Afraid of the Name ‘Taiwan Pavilion,” the coalition of South Korean artists has criticized the biennale for disregarding artists’ right to identify their own nationality and failing to engage in discussion and consultation, and said it is deeply troubling that such “political censorship” occurred in Gwangju, a city known as South Korea’s “sacred ground of democracy.”
“The Taiwan Pavilion case reflects a broader problem in the international art world, where discrimination based on nationality, race, gender, religion or political views has led to artworks being altered or removed, exhibitions and public statements being canceled, and artists and cultural workers being silenced,” the group said.

title: Occupational health challenges require more than individual support, new doctoral study shows
content:
Mental health issues are now the most prevalent cause of sick leave in Finland. It is common for an employee's declining occupational well-being to result in a sick leave referral, while nothing changes at the workplace itself.
"When this happens, the symptoms tend to reappear after a while," says doctoral researcher Pinja Ryky of the University of Helsinki.
Ryky is calling for more collective methods of tackling coping problems in workplaces.
Management training focuses on individuals
Ryky's doctoral study looked at training given to managers to help them promote occupational well-being and solve related problems.
"The training approached the subject through the managers' own well-being, as well as mindfulness, or conscious presence. Such approaches disguise the organization's responsibilities in managing occupational well-being," says Ryky.
The study trialed a new approach in which both instructors and participants in management training explored occupational well-being development in the long term and from the perspective of the management system. Ultimately, however, the participants' attention remained fixed on individual traits rather than extending to the organizational level.
Collective support makes a difference
The study recommends enhancing managers' ability to identify occupational health problems. They should be able to determine when employees require individual support and when organizational practices must change.
Managers should also regularly tackle issues collectively. For instance, when increasing stress is observed within a workplace community, both the causes and necessary changes should be considered collectively.
Resolving problems together could ease managers' sense of isolation in the workplace.
"Framing occupational well-being as an individual's responsibility wears down managers as well, as it makes them personally responsible for both their own and their employees' well-being. In reality, managers also need the support of the community," says Ryky.
Ryky undertook her doctoral study as part of her role as a senior specialist at the Finnish Institute of Occupational Health.
"My own past experience of job burnout is what led me to take on the topic. The research has also shifted my thinking, and I now understand more clearly how work-life structures affect mental health."
Provided by University of Helsinki

title: From cashier to attorney: Pretoria woman set to open law firm
content:
At 27, Fortune Seloana is looking forward to opening her own law firm — but her long and difficult journey started with long shifts as a cashier for a retail store.
Seloana, from Pretoria, was admitted as an attorney last month after graduating from Unisa in 2023.
Her journey was not without challenges, as her manager at the shop made her life difficult when Seloana told her that she would need time off to study for her exams. At the time she had been working as a cashier there for about five months and management had not been aware she was studying law.
As her exams approached, she printed her timetable and handed it to her supervisor, requesting two days off — the day before each exam and the day of the exam.
But while she waited outside the manager’s office, she heard him talking to another person questioning why Seloana was working at the store if she was studying law.
“I could hear him from outside the office shouting, saying, ‘If she’s studying law, what is she doing here?’” she recalled.
For Seloana, that moment changed her experience at the store and things got worse as she pushed to work the floor of the shop by assisting customers with items they wanted to buy.
“I knew that it was just about to get worse,” she said.
She resigned about a month after requesting the study leave.
Long hours
Seloana said the difficult working conditions did not stop her from pursuing her studies. The store opened at about 6am and she would work until about 9pm, leaving little time for studying. “I knew that every day after work I had to dedicate at least an hour of my time to study before I could sleep,” she explained.
Her determination was driven by more than the prospect of a qualification. Seloana said she took the retail job to gain experience and learn independence. “I didn’t really need the money, but I was working for experience first of all. I’ve always been one person who wanted to learn about independence at a young age.”
After completing her degree in 2023, she spent two years as a candidate attorney, gaining experience in criminal and civil matters and spending much of her time in court. “I was admitted as an attorney in July and I am now in the process of opening my own law firm, where I intend to specialise in civil matters, including divorce, maintenance and human rights cases.”
For others who are studying while working, she advises them to find a balance but not lose sight of their education. “One hour a day is better than nothing ... If it is not working, choose your studies over the employment. At the end of the day, you don’t want to be there for years and only realise later that you should have chosen your studies.”
Seloana said it took her nine years to reach the point she is at today — a period she believes should not discourage anyone.
“Whether you decide to do something with your life, for 10 years or not, at the end of the day, that 10 years will pass. You have to choose whether, when that 10 years comes, you want it to find you in the same position or you want it to find you at a better level.”
Her faith has also remained central throughout her journey. “God always provides. I’ve always lived with those words. God will always provide,” she added.

title: Impact of Metformin Plus Lifestyle Intervention Compared With Lifestyle Intervention Alone on Prediabetes Remission in Participants With Impaired Glucose Regulation: The China DPP Study.
content: Prediabetes affects 35% of Chinese adults and is associated with increased risks of cardiovascular disease and mortality. However, findings are inconsistent on the effects of lifestyle and pharmacological interventions in the prediabetes population achieving remission. This analysis aimed to compare the effects of metformin plus lifestyle intervention versus lifestyle intervention alone for prediabetes remission. This was a secondary analysis of the China Diabetes Prevention Program (CDPP), a multicentre unblinded randomised controlled trial of 1678 participants aged 18-70 years with impaired glucose regulation from 43 hospitals across China (NCT03441750). Participants were randomly assigned (1:1) using block randomisation stratified by glucose status (impaired fasting glucose or impaired glucose tolerance), presence of hypertension and use of anti-hypertensive medication. They received either metformin plus lifestyle intervention or lifestyle intervention alone for 2 years. The primary outcome was prediabetes remission rate. During a median follow-up of 2.03 years, remission was achieved in 262/831 (31.5%) (138/396 men; 124/435 women) participants in the metformin plus lifestyle group versus 213/847 (25.1%) (106/397 men; 107/450 women) in the lifestyle alone group, with similar effects across subgroups. After adjusting for baseline characteristics, addition of metformin increased the rate of remission (HR 1.39, 95% CI 1.16-1.67, p < 0.001). Higher baseline HbA1c was associated with lower remission rates (HR 0.23, 95% CI 0.18-0.29, p < 0.001). Adding metformin to a lifestyle intervention significantly improved prediabetes remission rates over lifestyle intervention alone in Chinese adults with impaired glucose regulation. This may be an effective approach for prediabetes management.

title: Texas law banning drag shows where children may be present struck down again
content:
A federal judge has, for a second time, struck down a Texas state law banning drag performances in settings where children may be present.
In a ruling issued on Tuesday, US district judge David Hittner said Texas cannot enforce its drag show ban. He said that the measure improperly restricts speech and violates the first amendment of the US constitution.
The Texas ban, known as Senate bill 12, was passed in March 2023 and bans drag performers from dancing suggestively or wearing certain prosthetics on public property or in front of children, or “sexually-oriented performance” presented on the premises in the presence of an individual younger than 18 years of age.
Advocacy groups sued the state after the bill’s passage, arguing the ban on “sexually oriented performance” infringed on constitutional rights. Texas’s move was just one across several states in 2023, driven by a right-wing backlash to increasing queer and transgender rights and equality. Hittner initially declared the ban unconstitutional in September 2023, but it was unblocked by the 5th US circuit court of appeals in 2025, which returned the case to the judge.
That allowed Texas attorney general, Ken Paxton, who is locked in a race for a US Senate seat against Democrat James Talarico, to resume enforcing the law earlier this year.
The new ruling prevents Paxton from enforcing the law. Paxton said he would appeal the decision. “This is a profoundly flawed decision that endangers our children and is an affront to Texas values,” Paxton on X.
In his ruling, Hittner advised anyone “who find such activities as described in this case offensive” to “just don’t go”.
The ruling mentioned Dolly Parton, who died on Tuesday, when it critiqued the law’s definition of banning performances that “appeal to the prurient interest”. Hittner cited people who would chastise Parton “as a voluptuous sex symbol because of her big hair, flamboyant clothes and breast exposure”.
“There are ‘erotic’ elements in countless popular performances that could be subject to both civil and criminal penalties under SB 12,” Hittner wrote.
Hittner said the terms used in the legislation were so broad they could block performers like Lady Gaga or Miley Cyrus from performing in the state.
“Even if S.B. 12 were somehow content-neutral (an argument the Attorney General has never advanced), it still prohibits huge swaths of constitutionally protected performances. Because the term ‘prurient interest in sex’ is open-ended, SB 12 can be used to cherry-pick particular aspects of performances that might be ‘in some sense erotic’,” Hittner wrote.
He said that because the law was very broad it caused some everyday activities, including “cheerleading, dancing, live theater, and other common public occurrences” to be regarded as civil or criminal violations. He also said that the law was vague on its face and that it failed “to give a reasonable person notice of what is prohibited”.
Civil liberties groups welcomed the ruling. “Drag has a rich history as a refuge of joy and liberation for countless Texans, and it’s not going anywhere,” said the Texas chapter of the ACLU in a statement.
“All Texans – no matter our gender or background – are guaranteed the right to free expression,” it added.
Brigitte Bandit, a plaintiff in the case who impersonates Parton, celebrated the ruling on social media. “Drag is free speech, b----.” She announced she would also perform as Parton, who gave her a rhinestone guitar as a gift in 2023, at an Austin bar Saturday in her honor.
